SUP-s109-supp xe:RAND:0:5:w17 step 31 (pass), xe:RAND:1:9:w10 step 21, w11 step 16, w12 step 25, w14 step 25, w15 step 21, w16 step 21 and xe:RAND:2:11:w18 step 33: gorge [] vs xmage [ability:Laboratory Drudge@p0] (some windows p1); Forge agrees with gorge (both suppress). Oracle text: "At the beginning of each end step, draw a card if you've cast a spell from a graveyard or activated an ability of a card in a graveyard this turn." The "if" follows the effect, not the trigger condition, so CR 603.4 does not make it an intervening-if: "A triggered ability may read 'When/Whenever/At [trigger event], if [condition], [effect].' When the trigger event occurs, the ability checks whether the stated condition is true. The ability triggers only if it is; otherwise it does nothing. ... This rule is referred to as the 'intervening if clause' rule. (The word 'if' has only its normal English meaning anywhere else in the text of a card; this rule only applies to an 'if' that immediately follows a trigger condition.)" The 2020-11-10 ruling: "Laboratory Drudge's ability will trigger at the beginning of each end step whether you've cast a spell from a graveyard or activated an ability of a card in a graveyard that turn or not." The ability must trigger every end step and check the condition at resolution; XMage's ConditionalOneShotEffect on LaboratoryDrudge.java:32-37 (condition at resolution) is correct. Gorge and Forge are wrong: .cards/cardsfolder/l/laboratory_drudge.txt:5 puts CheckSVar$ NumCast on the T:Mode$ Phase line, and gorge engine/rules/trigger_condition.go:423-461 reads CheckSVar as an intervening-if.
